viewer_sees: SILHOUETTE — a file of gods carrying a heavy coiled chain along a black ridge toward a seated wolf shape on the skyline; the shadow the wolf throws down the slope is several times longer than the wolf itself

MACRO OBJECT — a weathered carved memorial stone: a wolf figure at its centre bound by a carved chain; the camera pushes in until the carving fills the frame, the carved chain splits, and the carved sun and carved hall behind it break into pieces

TIMELINE — one locked framing of the hall doorway with gods watching from the near shadow; on each pass the wolf in the doorway is larger, the light runs green to grey to snow, and the door frame splinters wider around him
Læding wound in heavy coils around the wolf's chest and shoulders; he braces low, the links draw straight and thin at the strain, then burst and whip away across the rock
the same framing as the first attempt but with Drómi, visibly twice as thick, dragged into place by several gods; the wolf rises against it and the reinforced links tear open the same way
EMPTY AFTERMATH — the churned ground where the wolf stood: two burst chains half-sunk in mud, deep claw furrows filling with rainwater, one abandoned spear; NOT IN FRAME: the wolf, the gods
PROCESS CUTAWAY — the forge shown in cross-section: coal beds glowing in the lower chamber, the dwarfs at the anvil above drawing out a thread finer than a hair instead of hammering iron

MACRO OBJECT — the finished ribbon coiled on a dwarf's open palm, near-camera and weightless enough to lift on a breath; behind it, far and out of focus, a single burst iron link from Drómi as wide as the whole hand

LEDGER / ACCUMULATION — six impossible things drawn one after another into a braiding thread: a cat's soundless print, a root under a mountain, a bear's sinew, a fish's breath, a bird's spittle, a woman's beard, each dissolving into the strand as it joins and the strand growing no thicker
the gods hold the thin ribbon out on the open rock; the wolf circles it at a distance, head low and ears flat, glancing back at the two burst chains still lying where they fell
the wolf lies down deliberately and holds his jaws wide open, waiting; the gods stand in a half-circle just beyond the reach of the teeth, none of them moving
the half-circle holds still and no one steps out of it; then Týr breaks the line, walks in alone, and lays his right hand flat between the open jaws
the gods pass the ribbon around the wolf in quick loops; he throws his weight against it, hind legs driving, the thread cutting a bright line into his fur — and it holds without stretching
the wolf stops straining and turns his eyes to the gods as he works it out; the jaws close; Týr's shoulder drops and he steps back with his forearm ending at the wrist

EMPTY AFTERMATH — the flat rock where Týr knelt: his bronze arm-ring lying on the stone, a dark stain spreading from a handprint, the ribbon's slack end nearby; NOT IN FRAME: Týr, the wolf, the other gods
TIMELINE — one locked framing of the bound wolf on the island; the light runs through summer, snow and thaw and back again, the ribbon never slackening, the wolf's eyes open in every state
SILHOUETTE — the bound wolf black against a low grey sky, framed as in the opening shot; at this distance the thread is invisible, so nothing appears to be holding him at all
MACRO OBJECT — the three bindings laid side by side on wet stone: Læding burst, Drómi burst, and the thin ribbon whole and still taut, with a bronze arm-ring set beside them
